question_en:
I am compiling a supplementary archive of posters and performance photos for the stage production in the attachment. Please answer the following questions:

1. Which production does the poster advertise? What are the host city, specific venue, and event? What are the date, reproduction number, and call number in the Library of Congress catalog record?
2. Which three cities did this production visit in sequence? List them in chronological order.
3. The Library of Congress held a theater-themed exhibition from February 17 to July 16, 2011. In the online image Gallery of this exhibition, locate the image set corresponding to the production shown in the attachment. Use a table to list the sequence number of each image within this set and whether it meets the criteria. Images meeting the criteria must simultaneously include one of the following: a stage opening, a curtain, or identifiable stage scenery, and must feature at least two performers in costume. How many images are there in total under this production, and how many meet the criteria?

Response Format: Answer in numbered points (1)–(3). For Question 1, use a two-column table with headers "Item" and "Answer" to list the requested information. For Question 2, list the three cities in order using text. For Question 3, use a table to list the sequence and judgment for each image, and provide a single sentence stating the total number of images and the number that meet the criteria.

# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 8-3-A02

## Step 01 · Extract production and location from the poster

**Action**: Read the large text on the current poster and the event name at the bottom; example query: "Swing Mikado" "Treasure Island" Library of Congress.

**Evidence Observation**: Readable text includes SWING MIKADO, FEDERAL THEATRE, TREASURE ISLAND, Golden Gate International Exposition; also visible is "HOT FROM NEW YORK". "Starting June15th" is only a promotional date and cannot alone determine the catalog publication year.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/98517765/

**Result of this step**: Use the production name and location together to search for the official poster record.

## Step 02 · Verify identity fields in the official catalog

**Action**: Access Library of Congress item 98517765, and transcribe verbatim the catalog date, reproduction number, and call number.

**Evidence Observation**: The catalog record identifies the location as San Francisco, California, the specific venue as Treasure Island, and the event as Golden Gate International Exposition; the date field is [California : Federal Art Project, 1939 or 1940], preserving its either-or uncertainty. Reproduction number LC-USZC2-5540, call number POS - WPA - CA .01 .S787, no. 1 (C size) [P&P].

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/98517765/

**Result of this step**: The poster identity and catalog fields are confirmed; do not arbitrarily simplify to 1939.

## Step 03 · Trace the production's city tour

**Action**: Combine the production transfer narrative from the official Federal Theatre historical article with the poster's destination.

**Evidence Observation**: The article supports the chronological sequence from Chicago to New York; the poster states it is a successful production from New York and marks the performance location as Treasure Island in San Francisco. Connecting these two sources yields Chicago → New York → San Francisco.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.loc.gov/collections/federal-theatre-project-1935-to-1939/articles-and-essays/federal-theatre-melodrama-social-protest-and-genius/

https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/98517765/

**Result of this step**: Obtain the chronological order of the three cities.

## Step 04 · Close the image set within the specified historical exhibition

**Action**: Locate the theater exhibition Gallery held from February 17 to July 16, 2011, read the consecutive images under the Swing Mikado heading, and stop at the next production heading.

**Evidence Observation**: The archived Gallery contains 14 images for this production. The full set includes posters, guests, stage shots, and studio portraits; one must not retain only those members that appear to be performances based on the title or thumbnail appearance; additional materials from the finding aid are not included in this set.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/federal-theatre-project/gallery.html

**Result of this step**: Fix the sequence as 1–14; do not expand the search to other same-named images across the entire library.

**Action**: For each image separately, judge stage element A and at least two performers in costume B, then calculate A and B.

**Evidence Observation**: A stage opening, a curtain, or identifiable stage scenery satisfies any one of condition A; condition B requires at least two people in costume. The prompt does not require them to be performing, so a group photo of actors in front of a curtain may qualify; conversely, studio portraits with many actors cannot bypass condition A.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/federal-theatre-project/gallery.html

**Result of this step**: Record the two conditions separately to reduce misjudgment of group photos and studio portraits.
